diagnostic_evidence.quote: Solving the (discretized) local eigenproblem \cref{eq:gevp} requires calculating a basis for the local $B$-harmonic space.

issues.failure_explanation: Let the full local space have dimension n and the zero-artificial-boundary test space dimension m. Local well-posedness makes the harmonic constraint have rank m, so the original eigenproblem in a harmonic basis has n−m independent unknowns. The mixed problem has n+m unknowns. On refined regular meshes these scale respectively like boundary and volume degrees of freedom, so their ratio grows like H/h rather than approaching two. Avoiding harmonic-basis construction can still be beneficial, but the stated size comparison does not establish that benefit.

failure_location.quote: Although this alternative formulation of the eigenproblem has almost twice as many unknowns as the original problem, it is not only more convenient for the implementation due to its formulation on standard spaces, but also computationally cheaper.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Give the dimensions n−m and n+m explicitly, distinguish ambient nodal storage from independent harmonic coordinates, and qualify the cost comparison using the work avoided in harmonic-basis construction.
issues.overall_effect: The computational-size comparison and its supporting explanation of the mixed formulation's cost are materially misstated.
issues.title: The mixed eigenproblem is not merely twice the size of the harmonic-space eigenproblem
issues.why_classification: The repair changes a constant-factor comparison into a mesh-dependent one and requires revising the cost justification, but leaves the mixed construction and approximation theory intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (cf.\ \cref{th:msgfem:evaldecay} below, where an exponential decay is shown)

issues.failure_explanation: The cited theorem supplies only an upper envelope for individual eigenvalues, not a lower bound on their separation. It permits repeated eigenvalues and arbitrarily small gaps. Even the exact sequence λ_k=exp(−2c k^(1/d)) has relative consecutive gaps tending to zero for d=2 or 3. Thus the displayed decay estimate cannot justify the asserted gap-based eigensolver acceleration.

failure_location.quote: iterative solvers for this eigenproblem typically converge fast since the relative spectral gaps between consecutive eigenvalues are large

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the conclusion to spectral-tail decay and make eigensolver acceleration conditional on quantitative spectral separation, or supply a separate gap and eigensolver analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed theoretical rationale for fast local eigensolver convergence is unsupported; the coarse-space approximation estimate itself is not defeated by this inference.
issues.title: Eigenvalue-tail decay does not establish large relative spectral gaps
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the computational claim resolves the defect without changing the preconditioner or spectral approximation theory.

issues.failure_explanation: Take Ω=(0,6)×(0,ε), A=I, velocity zero, Dirichlet conditions on the two vertical ends and outflow/Neumann conditions on the horizontal sides. Set D**=(1,5)×(0,ε), D*=(2,4)×(0,ε), and D=(2.5,3.5)×(0,ε). All stated geometric conditions hold with δ=1, and 1 and x_1 belong to H_B(D**). For sufficiently small ε, N=1 satisfies the threshold. Applying the estimate to 1 forces the one-dimensional approximation space to restrict to constants on D*. Its error for x_1 is of order √ε, whereas the asserted right-hand side is at most of order ε. Dimension-only constants therefore cannot work, despite well-posed global and local problems.

failure_location.quote: Then, there are constants $C_1$, $C_2 > 0$ depending only on $\dimDomain$ such that for every integer $N \geq C_1 \abs{D^{**}}\delta^{-\dimDomain}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce geometric Poincaré/extension constants for boundary-intersecting domains, prove the approximation estimate with those constants, and propagate them through the spectral and convergence estimates. Alternatively, impose an explicit uniform geometric condition sufficient for that estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The stated weak approximation property is false for allowed boundary-truncated domains. The subsequent framework applications and their quantitative constants require a valid replacement property.
issues.title: The weak approximation constants cannot depend only on dimension
issues.why_classification: A contained geometric approximation lemma and revised constants can preserve the spectral-decay exponent and convergence framework; dimension-only uniformity must be relinquished or supported by additional geometry.

issues.failure_explanation: Zero velocity is allowed and explicitly used. Then both the numerator and denominator of the displayed quotient vanish. Multiplication by the zero Péclet number does not define the resulting expression, so the promised explicit C_j is not a number in the pure-diffusion case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write the first term in unfactored form, (H_j/a_min)√(||b||∞²+a_min||div b||∞), or explicitly define its zero-velocity extension to be zero.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant formula does not cover an included parameter case, although the qualitative spectral-decay theorem need not fail there.
issues.title: The quantified spectral prefactor is undefined for zero velocity
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic reformulation handles the degenerate case without changing any estimate, rate, or parameter regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If  $\bilWF{\cdot}{\cdot}{}$ is coercive or $\evalMax$ and $H^*_{\mathrm{max}}$ are sufficiently small, then
For coercive $\bilB$ the estimate follows immediately from \cite[Theorem 3.20]{Ma2025}.

issues.failure_explanation: For mere coercivity B(v,v)≥α_B||v||_a², the Galerkin quasi-optimality argument introduces the continuity constant divided by α_B, not the continuity constant alone. Unit coercivity follows in the divergence-free case, but is not assumed here. For example, with full Dirichlet boundary, A=I and b=−t x, B(v,v)=||∇v||²−td||v||²/2; its coercivity constant can approach zero while the coefficient norms in the stated C_B remain bounded. No uniform stability estimate eliminating this dependence is supplied.

failure_location.quote: where $C_B \sim 1 + \diffMin^{-1}\left(\norm{\divergence \velField}_{\Lp{\infty}} + \norm{\velField}_{\Lpd{\infty}}\right)$ is the operator norm of the bilinear form $\bilWF{\cdot}{\cdot}{}$ up to coefficient-independent constants.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the actual inverse coercivity constant in the coercive branch, or strengthen that branch to a stated uniform lower bound such as B(v,v)≥||v||_a².
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional quantitative bound for general coercive problems is not established. The divergence-free specialization does not suffer from this particular missing factor.
issues.title: General coercivity does not give the stated quasi-optimality constant
issues.why_classification: The repair preserves quasi-optimality and exponential convergence but necessarily changes the coefficient dependence of the advertised bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout this paper, we assume that the global problem as well as all occurring subdomain problems are well-posed.

issues.failure_explanation: No positive-measure Dirichlet boundary or other global Poincaré condition is imposed. Well-posedness does not supply one: on the unit ball, take Γ_D empty, Γ_O the whole boundary, A=I and b=x. Then B is coercive in H¹, since B(v,v)=||∇v||²+d||v||²/2+||v||²_boundary/2. Nevertheless ||1||_a=0 while B(1,1)=|∂Ω|>0. Thus B has no finite continuity norm relative to the energy seminorm used in the stated quasi-optimality estimate. This is independent of the missing coercivity factor.

failure_location.quote: is the operator norm of the bilinear form $\bilWF{\cdot}{\cdot}{}$ up to coefficient-independent constants.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State a global Poincaré hypothesis, for example a Dirichlet part of positive surface measure, for this analysis. To retain outflow-only problems, use a norm controlling constants and rederive the global estimate in that norm.
issues.overall_effect: The global energy-norm justification does not cover allowed, well-posed outflow-only problems.
issues.title: The global energy-norm argument lacks a condition controlling constants
issues.why_classification: A limited boundary-regime restriction repairs the existing argument; retaining the full stated boundary scope requires a substantive norm and estimate revision.

issues.failure_explanation: Divergence-free convection gives the needed local coercivity on functions vanishing on the artificial boundary, not on all of H¹_D(ω_j*). The harmonic error generally has nonzero artificial-boundary trace. On an interior rectangle with A=I and b=(β,0), e=exp(βx_1) is B-harmonic and has positive energy, but B_D(e,e)=0 pointwise after cancellation of diffusion and convection. It can be realized as the stated local error by choosing a global solution equal to e on the patch and forcing supported outside it. The subsequent gradient-only continuity estimate also lacks the boundary condition needed for its Poincaré step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a local projection-stability lemma instead. Decompose u using the a-orthogonal projection onto H¹_{D,0}; apply coercivity only to the zero-trace correction and use a-orthogonality to bound the harmonic remainder. This yields a bound of the required 1+C Pe_H form without applying coercivity to the harmonic error.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on the local harmonic error in terms of the global solution energy, and hence the supplied contraction proof, is unsupported.
issues.title: Local coercivity is applied to an error with nonzero artificial-boundary trace
issues.why_classification: A contained nontrivial projection argument can preserve the intended local estimate and downstream convergence architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Estimate \cref{eq:msgfem:global:coercive} then follows from \cref{eq:msgfem:global} and the definition of $\colConst^*$.

issues.failure_explanation: Even granting the preceding local projection estimate, substitution into the global theorem gives C_B(1+C Pe_H), not (1+C Pe_H)². The global continuity norm depends on the global domain scale; it cannot generally be bounded by a local-scale expression tending to one as uniformly shaped subdomains shrink. No localized Galerkin estimate replacing the global continuity norm is proved. This gap survives correction of the erroneous local-coercivity argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain C_B(1+C Pe_H) in the corollary, or supply a separate localized global error argument that genuinely proves the stronger local-scale prefactor.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit squared local-Péclet prefactor is not established. Existence of arbitrarily small contraction factors would still follow from a correct finite prefactor and eigenvalue decay.
issues.title: The global continuity factor is replaced by a local Péclet factor without justification
issues.why_classification: Keeping C_B is a supported limited weakening of the quantitative estimate; preserving the stronger prefactor requires a contained additional argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Every correction produced by G has zero trace on Γ_D, so the iteration preserves the initial Dirichlet trace. The approximation estimate for homogeneous-boundary solutions cannot be applied to arbitrary H¹ functions. For A=I, b=0, full Dirichlet boundary and u^e=0 on a square, take u^(0)=x_1. This function is globally and locally harmonic, so all local projections and the coarse projection vanish. The iteration remains x_1 forever, with positive energy error, regardless of coarse-space size.

failure_location.quote: converges for any initial guess $\fwp^{(0)} \in \Hone$ strictly monotonically:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the contraction on H¹_D(Ω) and require the initial guess to satisfy the homogeneous essential boundary condition, or enforce that trace before starting the iteration.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted all-H¹ operator contraction and initial-guess guarantee are false.
issues.title: Convergence cannot hold for arbitrary H¹ initial guesses
issues.why_classification: Using the already-defined admissible trial space is a short boundary-compatibility repair that preserves the method and its convergence rate for the PDE's admissible iterates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix representation of the discretized MS-GFEM map $\msgfemOperator$ can thus be written as $\mat{\msgfemOperator} = \discPreconditioner\discBilForm$ with the preconditioner

issues.failure_explanation: Let L denote the one-level local inverse sum and C the coarse inverse. The printed definition is M=L+C(I−L). However, the continuous map and the two executable RAS steps give M=L+C(I−BL): after adding Lr, the coarse residual is r−BLr. Consequently the printed M does not satisfy the claimed matrix representation of G and does not implement the stated split iteration.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert B immediately before the local inverse sum in the coarse residual factor, giving M=L+C(I−BL), and use this definition consistently in the discrete iteration and GMRES system.
issues.overall_effect: Two different preconditioners are specified, and the displayed matrix definition does not inherit the advertised MS-GFEM/RAS correspondence.
issues.title: The displayed hybrid preconditioner omits the stiffness matrix in the residual update
issues.why_classification: The correct construction is already supplied by the two RAS steps; one local matrix-factor correction reconciles all representations without changing the intended algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's nonnegative negative-part convention, the prescribed inflow flux is −(b·ν)^− g on the left-hand side, hence +(b·ν)^− g on the right-hand side. The printed load instead contributes its negative. For constant divergence-free velocity and the exact constant solution u=g=c, the printed DG residual contains 2c times the inflow integral of (b·ν)^−v. In the zero-diffusion test it imposes the opposite inflow data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the plus sign before the negative-part term inside the load's bracket to a minus sign, and verify that reported runs use this consistent load.
issues.overall_effect: The stated DG scheme is inconsistent with the governing Dirichlet data, including the nonzero-inflow numerical examples.
issues.title: The DG load has the wrong sign for prescribed inflow data
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction restores the intended upwind boundary flux without changing the matrix, preconditioner construction, or convergence theory.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We choose the rotating velocity field

issues.failure_explanation: Writing X=x_1−0.5 and Y=x_2−0.5, the specified divergence is −80XY−3, which takes both positive and negative values on the square. At the centre the velocity Jacobian is [[−1.5,20],[20,−1.5]], with eigenvalues 18.5 and −21.5: the centre is a saddle, not a rotating sink. Opposite signs in the two cross-components would describe a different field and require deciding which experiment was intended.

failure_location.quote: which has negative divergence and yields an indefinite problem

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the specified field as having sign-changing divergence and a central saddle, and revise the experiment's interpretation accordingly. If a rotating compressive field was intended, correct the field and repeat or verify the associated experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The large-scale experiment does not establish performance for the particular everywhere-negative-divergence rotating flow advertised by its description. It can still be an indefinite, non-divergence-free test.
